segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Okay, let's get started. This is our go, no-go review for the Meridian launch. Marcus, Elena, thanks for making time.

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: Happy to be here. I've got the engineering status ready whenever you want it.

segments.speaker: Elena
segments.text: Same on the marketing side. I'll follow after Marcus.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Perfect. Marcus, why don't you start with where the build stands.

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: Sure. As of this morning, the release candidate is code complete and it's been in staging for four days.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: And how's it holding up?

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: Mostly well. We found two P2 bugs during regression, both already fixed and verified.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Any P1s or P0s?

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: One P1, still open. It's an intermittent crash on the checkout confirmation screen, only on older Android devices.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Do we understand the cause yet?

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: We think so. It looks like a race condition when the payment confirmation comes back before the animation finishes.

segments.speaker: Elena
segments.text: How intermittent are we talking? Once in a hundred sessions, once in a thousand?

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: Closer to one in three hundred, based on the crash reporting from the beta cohort.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: That's not nothing. What's the fix estimate?

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: Our best guess is a day of work plus half a day of testing, so realistically ready by tomorrow evening.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Okay. Let's treat that as a blocker for now and revisit at the end of this meeting.

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: Agreed, that's fair.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: What about performance? Last time we talked, cold start was still a concern.

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: Good news there. We shaved off about four hundred milliseconds by lazy loading the onboarding illustrations.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: What's cold start sitting at now?

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: Around one point eight seconds on our reference device, down from two point three.

segments.speaker: Elena
segments.text: That's a nice win. Does that apply evenly across low end devices too, or mostly flagship phones?

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: Mostly flagship so far. We haven't finished profiling on the budget Android tier yet.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Can we get that data before the launch decision?

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: I can have preliminary numbers by tomorrow morning, full numbers by end of day tomorrow.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Let's aim for the preliminary numbers, that should be enough to make the call.

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: Sounds good, I'll prioritize that first thing.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Anything else on engineering before we move to marketing?

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: Just one thing. The analytics team asked for two new events to be added before launch, and those are already merged.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Great, thanks Marcus. Elena, over to you.

segments.speaker: Elena
segments.text: Thanks. On the marketing side, the campaign assets are finished and approved by legal as of yesterday.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: That's ahead of schedule, nice.

segments.speaker: Elena
segments.text: We got lucky, legal turned it around in two days instead of the usual week.

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: Did the messaging change at all during legal review?

segments.speaker: Elena
segments.text: Only minor wording. We had to soften one claim about battery savings to say, quote, up to thirty percent, unquote.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Makes sense, that's safer language anyway. What's the plan for launch day itself?

segments.speaker: Elena
segments.text: We're doing a staggered rollout. Email to the waitlist at nine AM, social posts at ten, and a press embargo lifts at noon.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: How big is the waitlist at this point?

segments.speaker: Elena
segments.text: Just under forty thousand people, which is about twenty percent higher than we projected in August.

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: That's a good problem to have. Are we confident the backend can handle a spike from that many people at once?

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Good question. Marcus, do we have load testing numbers for that scenario?

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: We load tested up to sixty thousand concurrent sign ups last week and it held, but I'd want to rerun it since the checkout fix hasn't landed.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Let's rerun load testing tomorrow once the checkout fix is in.

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: Will do.

segments.speaker: Elena
segments.text: One more thing on my side. We have three press outlets confirmed for early access briefings this week.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Which outlets?

segments.speaker: Elena
segments.text: TechDaily, the Morning Ledger, and a smaller newsletter called Signal Weekly that's popular with our target audience.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Good spread. Any concerns from them so far?

segments.speaker: Elena
segments.text: TechDaily asked about pricing changes for existing customers, so we should make sure support has clean talking points.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Let's make sure that's in the support brief. Speaking of which, where do we stand on support readiness?

segments.speaker: Elena
segments.text: I don't own that directly, but I know the support team finished their training session yesterday.

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: I can speak to the technical side. We gave them a runbook for the top ten expected issues, including the checkout bug once it's fixed.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Good. Let's make sure that runbook gets updated the moment the fix ships, not after.

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: Understood, I'll own that update myself so it doesn't slip.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Thank you. Let's talk about the launch date itself. Original target was this Thursday.

segments.speaker: Elena
segments.text: From a marketing standpoint, Thursday still works. All the assets are locked and the press embargo is already scheduled.

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: From engineering, I'd feel more comfortable with Friday, just to give the checkout fix a full day of soak time after it ships.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: That's a reasonable ask. Elena, how disruptive would a one day slip be for marketing?

segments.speaker: Elena
segments.text: Not too bad. We'd need to reschedule the press embargo and resend one calendar invite, but nothing structural breaks.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Okay, let's tentatively move to Friday, pending the checkout fix landing cleanly tomorrow.

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: That works for me.

segments.speaker: Elena
segments.text: Agreed, I'll start adjusting the press calendar today so it's ready either way.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Let's talk risk register quickly before we wrap. Marcus, top risk from your side?

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: Still the checkout crash. Second would be the unknown performance on budget Android devices.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: And a mitigation for the Android question if the numbers come back bad?

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: Worst case, we feature flag the new onboarding illustrations off for lower end devices and keep the old flow there.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Good, that's a reasonable fallback. Elena, top risk from marketing?

segments.speaker: Elena
segments.text: Honestly, it's the waitlist size. If sign up traffic spikes harder than expected, a rocky first hour could hurt press sentiment.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: That lines up with wanting fresh load test numbers. Let's make sure those are done before Friday regardless of which day we launch.

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: Agreed, I'll treat that as non negotiable before go live.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Good. Let's also touch on the rollback plan in case something goes wrong on launch day.

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: We can roll back the client release within about fifteen minutes since it's a staged rollout, not a hard cutover.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: And on the backend?

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: Backend changes are backward compatible with the previous client version, so a rollback there is low risk.

segments.speaker: Elena
segments.text: What would trigger a rollback decision, and who makes that call on launch day?

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Good question. Let's say crash rate above two percent or checkout failure rate above five percent triggers an automatic page to me and Marcus.

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: That threshold matches what we used for the last major release, so it's a reasonable bar.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Agreed. Let's put that in writing in the launch runbook today so there's no ambiguity on the day.

segments.speaker: Elena
segments.text: I can help draft that section if it's useful, I've written similar runbooks before.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: That would be great, thank you.

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: One last engineering item. We should decide who's on call across the launch window, especially if we move to Friday.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Let's plan for you and one other engineer during business hours, plus normal on call coverage overnight.

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: I'll pull in Renata for the daytime shift, she's been closest to the checkout code this sprint.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Perfect, please loop her in today so she has context ahead of time.

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: Will do, I'll message her right after this call.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Elena, anything else from marketing before we close out?

segments.speaker: Elena
segments.text: Just a reminder that the influencer partnerships go live the same day as press, so timing really does matter here.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Understood, that's a strong argument for locking the date firmly by tomorrow afternoon.

segments.speaker: Elena
segments.text: Agreed, tomorrow afternoon works well for us.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Alright, let's summarize. Checkout fix ships and is verified tomorrow. Fresh load test and budget device numbers come in tomorrow too.

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: And the support runbook gets updated the moment the fix ships, not after.

segments.speaker: Elena
segments.text: And I'll have the press calendar ready to shift to Friday, plus a draft of the rollback section for the runbook.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Great. Let's reconvene tomorrow at the same time to make the final go, no-go call.

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: Works for me.

segments.speaker: Elena
segments.text: Same here, talk tomorrow.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Thanks both, this was a productive session.
